summary:
I checked every factual statement in im-script.txt against the claim ledger, the local snapshots, the scratch copies, and the Impro text itself. I re-opened Impro in the Google Books preview: Routledge 2012 (id EVmminvaWDQC) for pp.42-44, 46, 55 and snippet searches for pp.33, 36, 37, 97; A&C Black 2007 (id B2FO8HhgH-0C) for the open pages 94, 95, 97, 101. Verdict counts: 36 supported, 7 overreach, 1 wrong, 0 unsupported. Most of the segment is sound, and the Impro quotations, page claims and Qureshi/Mabrey wording hold up.

Statements to fix, in order of weight:
1. im.b19: "除了这两位，我没有找到别人讲过" is wrong against the series' own ledger. ov.karp_zamiska_book_via_reviews records two reviews (Robbins 2025-04-26, New Republic 2025-02-28) saying Karp and Zamiska's book reports Impro being given to or used by new hires. Mabrey's own paragraph says the explanation is in "their book". Safer wording: first-hand accounts only from these two; the Karp and Zamiska book reportedly covers it, but its text was not read.
2. im.i1: "公司寄这本书，是因为它把人的社会行为拆成了机制" turns Qureshi's "popular with nerds partly because..." into the company's reason for sending the book. His answer to "why Impro" is the FDE trust-and-social-context paragraph, which b17 correctly gives. The segment also drops "at the time when you joined" and "I'm not sure if they still do this".
3. im.b4: "之所以...正是因为" overstates Johnstone's "acquaintances become friends when they agree to play status games together".
4. im.b12: "锁住对手" mistranslates "lock on to the other actor". The repo's script.json has the faithful "紧紧盯住搭档". "靠的就是这套训练" turns "could never have toured successfully without" into a sole basis.
5. im.b15: "对自己的说法也有保留" is not in the source. p.42 concerns disagreement among other reports; p.55 concerns teaching resistance. The real hedge is "My belief (at this moment)", which b6 handles correctly.
6. im.b16: "说它让即兴变坏了" reads the journalist's juxtaposition as causation.

Labelling of the narrator's own readings: b2, b9, b16 and b19's "我的推论" are labelled. Two things are not. The "向外/向内" classification in b17 and b18 is the series' own framing, not Qureshi's or Mabrey's. The b19 sentence "这两种读法，都落在 Johnstone 那句话上" is the narrator's synthesis and sits before the "我的推论只到这里" marker, so it reads as fact. Neither source cites Johnstone's sentence, so the label should move up (the repo script.json puts "我自己的推论是" before it).

Note on versions: the reviewed text differs from palantir/reading-list-series/episodes/02-impro/script.json in 19 of 21 segments. The new b15 framing sentence, the b12 "锁住对手" and the b19 label placement are regressions from the repo version. No repository file was edited.

rows.statement: 上一集讲访谈，去听用户怎么说。
rows.source_locator: series-manifest.json assemblies ep01 next=im; unit iu = Portigal, Interviewing Users
rows.note: Series structure, not a source claim.

rows.statement: 这一集读 Impro，一本讲即兴戏剧的书。
rows.source_locator: vault/snapshots/local/palantir-20261006/johnstone-impro-publisher-page.html.txt line 1370; Google Books EVmminvaWDQC description ('Improvisation and the Theatre')

rows.statement: Qureshi 说，公司寄这本书。
rows.source_locator: vault/snapshots/local/palantir-20261006/qureshi-reflections-on-palantir.html.txt line 161: 'at the time when you joined they sent you a copy of Impro...'
rows.note: True as stated, but both of his limits are dropped: 'at the time when you joined' (he joined summer 2015) and 'I'm not sure if they still do this'. No other segment restores them, so the script gives an undated, unhedged 'the company sends it'.

rows.statement: ……是因为它把人的社会行为拆成了机制。
rows.source_locator: qureshi-reflections-on-palantir.html.txt line 163: 'Impro is popular with nerds partly because it breaks down social behavior mechanistically.'
rows.note: Qureshi says the book is popular with nerds partly because of this. He does not say it is why the company sent it. His answer to 'But why Impro?' is the preceding sentence: a successful FDE needs unusual sensitivity to social context and must gain counterparts' trust (the content of b17). The script makes the 'partly, popular with nerds' remark the company's reason, drops 'partly', and contradicts its own b17.

rows.statement: Johnstone 当过伦敦皇家宫廷剧院的副艺术总监。
rows.source_locator: Google Books EVmminvaWDQC publisher description: 'he was himself Associate Artistic Director'; ITI bio (scratch impro-collaboration/iti_about.txt line 34-35): 'Associate Director' of the Royal Court, 1956-66
rows.note: ITI says 'Associate Director'; the publisher text says 'Associate Artistic Director'. Both support 副艺术总监.

rows.statement: 在那里琢磨怎样让演员更自然、更有反应。
rows.source_locator: iti_about.txt line 35: 'With actors he began to explore how to make them more spontaneous, responsive and alive'
rows.note: 'spontaneous' is rendered 自然, not 自发 (the script's own chapter word in the next sentence). Small meaning shift; 自发 is closer. 'alive' is omitted.

rows.statement: 这本书初版于一九七九年。
rows.source_locator: keithjohnstone.com/writing caption '©1979, Methuen'; Google Books 'Originally published: 1979'; Wikipedia infobox 1979
rows.note: Sources disagree on the 1979 publisher (Methuen vs Faber), not on the year.

rows.statement: 分四个部分：地位，自发，讲故事，面具与恍惚。
rows.source_locator: johnstone-impro-publisher-page.html.txt line 1370; Google Books description: 'Divided into four sections, Status, Spontaneity, Narrative Skills, Masks and Trance'
rows.note: This is the publisher's wording. The Routledge contents page also lists Notes on Myself (p.13) and an Appendix (p.206).

rows.statement: 正文我能读到的，是出版社在谷歌图书上开放预览的那些页，集中在讲地位的一章。
rows.source_locator: Google Books EVmminvaWDQC ('Pages displayed by permission of Routledge'): full pages pp.42-44, 46, 50, 55-56; Status chapter runs pp.33-74 per contents list
rows.note: Accurate as a limit statement. Material for b13-b16 (pp.94-101) comes from snippets in the 2012 edition, but pp.94, 95, 97, 101 are open pages in the 2007 A&C Black preview (B2FO8HhgH-0C). 'Mainly this chapter' is therefore honest.

rows.statement: Johnstone 说的地位，不是一个人的社会身份，是他正在做的一件事。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.36 (snippet, search 'confusing term'): 'Status is a confusing term unless it's understood as something one does.'

rows.statement: 社会地位低的人，可以演出高地位，反过来也一样。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.36: 'You may be low in social status, but play high, and vice versa.'

rows.statement: 这种交易在现实里一刻也不停，并不只在起冲突的时候才有。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.33 (snippet, search 'continue all the time'): 'In reality status transactions continue all the time. In the park we'll notice the ducks squabbling, but not how carefully they keep their distances when they are not.'
rows.note: Clarity point: 'transaction' (交易) is never introduced in b3, so '这种交易' has no antecedent for a listener.

rows.statement: 有人反驳说，朋友之间总不玩地位吧。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.37 (snippet): 'Many people will maintain that we don't play status transactions with our friends...'

rows.statement: 他的回答是，熟人之所以成了朋友，正是因为双方同意一起玩地位的游戏。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.37 (snippets, searches 'acquaintances become friends' and 'status games together'): 'My answer is that acquaintances become friends when they agree to play status games together.'
rows.note: Source says 'when' (becoming friends coincides with agreeing to play status games). The script's 之所以...正是因为 makes agreement the cause. The same wording sits in the repo script.json. Suggested: 熟人变成朋友，是在双方同意一起玩地位游戏的时候。

rows.statement: 他把高和低各写成一句潜台词：演高地位的人在说「别靠近我，我会咬人」，演低地位的人在说「别咬我，我不值得你费劲」。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.43 (full page): 'A person who plays high status is saying "Don't come near me, I bite." Someone who plays low status is saying "Don't bite me, I'm not worth the trouble."'
rows.note: Quotation faithful. 'Subtext' (潜台词) is the script's gloss; Johnstone writes 'is saying'.

rows.statement: 他认为人各有偏好的地位，会设法挪到自己习惯的位置。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.43: 'people have a preferred status; that they like to be low, or high, and that they try to manoeuvre themselves into the preferred positions.'
rows.note: 'preferred' becomes 习惯 (habitual) in the second clause; slight drift from 偏好.

rows.statement: 说这话之前，他先加了一句：这是我此刻的看法。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.43: 'My belief (at this moment) is that...'
rows.note: Hedge preserved correctly.

rows.statement: 照他的说法，演出来的地位是一种防御，用惯了，人就被它定了型，被要求演另一种地位时，会觉得自己没了保护。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.43: 'the status played is a defence... It's very likely that you will increasingly be conditioned into playing the status that you've found an effective defence. You become a status specialist... Asked to play the "wrong" status, you'll feel "un-defended".'
rows.note: 'It's very likely' becomes flat 人就被它定了型; minor hardening, softened by 照他的说法.

rows.statement: 他上课时有一个演示：说话的时候让自己的头保持不动，然后告诉学生，这会改变他怎么看自己，也改变别人怎么看他。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.43: 'Finally I explain that I'm keeping my head still whenever I speak, and that this produces great changes in the way I perceive myself and am perceived by others.'
rows.note: 'great changes' is rendered 很明显地改变 ('obvious'), a small shift. It is Johnstone's own report of his own demonstration, not a measurement.

rows.statement: 头一不动，别的高地位动作会自己跟出来：说完整的句子，看着对方的眼睛，动作更顺，占的地方更大。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.44: 'If I speak with a still head, then I'll do many other high-status things quite automatically. I'll speak in complete sentences, I'll hold eye contact. I'll move more smoothly, and occupy more "space".'
rows.note: First-person report about himself. Johnstone calls these 'just tricks in order to get the students to experience status changes'.

rows.statement: 需要权威的角色，比如悲剧里的英雄，就得学会这一招；演掘墓人可以边说边晃脑袋，演哈姆雷特不行。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.43: 'Actors needing authority—tragic heroes and so on—have to learn this still head trick. You can talk and waggle your head about if you play the gravedigger, but not if you play Hamlet.'

rows.statement: Qureshi 在回忆里也转述过这类例子。
rows.source_locator: qureshi-reflections-on-palantir.html.txt line 163: head still = high status, head side to side = low; standing tall with hands showing = high; slouching, hands in pocket = low

rows.statement: 头不动这一条，书里找得到。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.43-44
rows.note: Only the still-head half is in the book. Qureshi's 'moving your head side to side is low status' is not a general rule in Johnstone; he ties head movement to stage roles (gravedigger vs Hamlet).

rows.statement: 他说的站直、露出双手，和驼背、手插口袋，我在能读到的书页里没有找到。
rows.source_locator: Impro pp.43-44 (full pages)
rows.note: Labelled as the narrator's own limit. Accurate for the exact pairing. pp.43-44 do give related examples (hands near vs away from face; toes inward vs sitting back and spreading).

rows.statement: 练习的时候，Johnstone 要求学生的地位只比搭档高一点，或者低一点。这样一来，学生就得真去看对方，照着对方的举动来调整自己。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.44: 'I insist that they have to get their status just a little above or below their partner's. This ensures that they really "see" their partner, as they have exactly to relate their behaviour to his.'

rows.statement: 他说，这些练习在台上重现的，正是现实里的情形：每个人每时每刻，都在把自己的地位往上或往下挪一点点。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.44: 'These status exercises reproduce on the stage exactly the effects of real life, in which moment by moment each person adjusts his status up or down a fraction.'
rows.note: His own assertion from teaching experience; no study cited.

rows.statement: 地位一旦练成了自动的反应，就会锁住对手，学生一下子变得很会观察。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.44: 'The automatic status skills then "lock on to" the other actor, and the students are transformed into observant, and apparently very experienced improvisers.'
rows.note: 'Lock on to the other actor' means the skills attach to the scene partner. 锁住对手 reads as pinning or trapping an opponent, and 对手 is not 搭档. The repo script.json has the faithful 紧紧盯住搭档. 'Apparently' (看上去) is also dropped.

rows.statement: 他的剧团能不排练就去欧洲巡演，他说靠的就是这套训练。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.46: 'Without the status work my improvisation group, the Theatre Machine, could never have toured successfully in Europe; not without preparing the scenes first.'
rows.note: The source gives a necessary condition (could not have toured successfully without it, not without preparing scenes first). 靠的就是 reads as the sole basis, and 'successfully' is dropped. Author's own account, no outside check.

rows.statement: 讲自发的那一章里，有一节讲接受和阻挡。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.94 section heading 'Blocking and Accepting' under running head SPONTANEITY (A&C Black 2007 preview); contents list: Spontaneity pp.75-108

rows.statement: 搭档的每个动作都可以看成一个提议，你可以接下，也可以挡回去。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.97 (A&C Black 2007 open page): 'I call anything that an actor does an "offer". Each offer can either be accepted, or blocked.'

rows.statement: Johnstone 说，阻挡是一种攻击。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.94: 'Blocking is a form of aggression.'
rows.note: His stated reason: given 'I love you' scenes, students almost always accept each other's ideas.

rows.statement: 多数学生更喜欢阻挡，而且常常没察觉自己在挡。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.95 (A&C Black 2007 open page): 'At first students don't realise when they're blocking or yielding... Some students prefer to yield (these are "charming" people) but most prefer to block, even though they may have no idea exactly what they are doing.'
rows.note: Two limits dropped: 'At first' and 'may'. Johnstone then stops improvisations to point the blocking out, so the unawareness is a starting condition.

rows.statement: 他举过一个例子：新手伸出手，想试试是不是下雨了，搭档却握住他的手，说，幸会。新手就恼了。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.101 'Blind Offers' (A&C Black 2007 open page): 'An inexperienced improviser gets annoyed because his partners misunderstand him. He holds out his hand to see if it's raining, and his partner shakes it and says "Pleased to meet you."'
rows.note: Facts correct. Framing risk: placed straight after 'blocking is aggression', it sounds like an example of blocking. The book files it under 'Blind Offers' as a misunderstanding, and the next lines are about making a blind offer that the partner accepts. The script never states the example's point.

rows.statement: 他要求演员别去想提议，而是假定对方已经给出了一个。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.99 (snippet; also quoted in scratch impro-collaboration/blevins.txt line 54): 'I tell my actors never to think up an offer, but instead to assume that one has already been made.'

rows.statement: Johnstone 对自己的说法也有保留。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.42 ('Such disagreements indicate the difficulty of actually perceiving status transactions'); p.55 (teaching resistance)
rows.note: Neither passage is a reservation about his own claims. p.42 concerns disagreement between other reports (an inventory finding vs a Stanford traffic-light experiment) and is followed by 'In my view...' asserted flatly. p.55 concerns the teaching situation. His actual hedge is 'My belief (at this moment)' on p.43, which b6 already covers. The sentence is new relative to the repo script.json and is the narrator's characterization, not marked as such.

rows.statement: 他承认，真要察觉地位的交易，并不容易。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.42: 'Such disagreements indicate the difficulty of actually perceiving status transactions.'
rows.note: Inferred from conflicting reports on eye contact and dominance.

rows.statement: 教这些东西，学生嘴上愿意，心里可能很抵触，得先让学生觉得安全。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.55: 'however willing the student is consciously, there may be very strong subconscious resistances. Making the student safe, and getting him to have confidence in you, are essential.'
rows.note: 嘴上愿意 suggests lip service; the source says consciously willing versus subconscious resistance. Minor nuance shift.

rows.statement: 一九七九年的书里，他写出色的即兴演员会接受对方给出的所有提议。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.99 (snippet; quoted in blevins.txt line 54): 'Good improvisers seem telepathic; everything looks prearranged. This is because they accept all offers made—which is something no "normal" person would do.'
rows.note: It is a description of what good improvisers do, not a rule. The text was read in the 2007/2012 reprints; the 1979 first printing was not compared.

rows.statement: 二〇〇七年接受采访时，他又把接受所有提议这条规则叫作一种扭曲。
rows.source_locator: Georgia Straight, 18 Jul 2007 (scratch impro-collaboration/straight_recants.txt, para 'Another of his beefs'): 'One mantra actors heed is "accept all offers"... He calls this particular rule a "perversion. I think it's terrible. Bad things have happened to improvisation."'
rows.note: A journalist's report of a phone call. Identifying the 'rule' as 'go wherever your cast mate takes you' is the journalist's wording, so the match with the 1979 sentence is plausible, not proven.

rows.statement: ……说它让即兴变坏了。
rows.source_locator: Georgia Straight 2007 (same paragraph)
rows.note: The quote is 'Bad things have happened to improvisation' after 'I think it's terrible'. The article does not state that the rule caused this, and the script turns the juxtaposition into causation. Low severity.

rows.statement: 两句话之间是什么关系，我没有找到他的解释。
rows.source_locator: Impro p.99 vs Georgia Straight 2007; scratch impro-collaboration/log.md section C: Canada's Theatre Museum 2017 interview part 18 on 'Yes, and' (description only, content unread)
rows.note: Labelled as the narrator's own limit. A relevant Johnstone interview exists but was not read, so 'not found' means 'not read', not 'none exists'.

rows.statement: Qureshi 的读法是向外的。
rows.source_locator: qureshi-reflections-on-palantir.html.txt line 163
rows.note: The outward/inward split is the series' own classification, not Qureshi's or Mabrey's wording, and the script does not label it as the narrator's reading. The substance fits both texts.

rows.statement: FDE 要在客户那里，跟最高层的对口人结成伙伴，取得信任，这常常要懂得玩政治。
rows.source_locator: qureshi-reflections-on-palantir.html.txt line 163: 'partner with your corporate (or government) counterparts at the highest level and gain their trust, which often required playing political games.'

rows.statement: 看不懂房间里的地位，就很难在客户那里站住。
rows.source_locator: qureshi-reflections-on-palantir.html.txt line 163: 'If you didn't know all this, you were unlikely to succeed in a customer environment. Which meant you were unlikely to integrate customer data or get people to use your software. Which meant failure.'
rows.note: 'All this' is Qureshi's paraphrase of Johnstone's physical high/low status. '房间' is the script's word (Qureshi uses 'reading rooms' in the next paragraph, about founders). 很难站住 is softer than his 'unlikely to succeed... failure'.

rows.statement: Ted Mabrey 的读法是向内的。
rows.source_locator: scratch overview/data/mabrey-techrepublic.clean.txt lines 20-21 (Mabrey, 2025-01-09)
rows.note: The inward label is the series' framing. Attribution caveat: the paragraph sits inside Mabrey's commentary on Karp and Zamiska's book. It says the explanation is given 'in their book', and the quoted fragments ('attribute not anything fixed or innate', 'require a union of the status that one is and the status that one plays') appear to be quoted from that book. 'Mabrey's reading' may be the authors' or company's account that he relays; the script does not say so.

rows.statement: 他写道，在 Palantir，人们被教导把地位看成一种用来推动局面的属性，不是界定一个人的东西。
rows.source_locator: mabrey-techrepublic.clean.txt line 21: 'At Palantir, we are taught we should view status as an attribute to use to advance a given situation, not an intrinsic property to define a person.'
rows.note: Present tense matches the source. The same paragraph says Impro was given to employees 'for many years' (past tense); the script does not say Mabrey's account is retrospective.

rows.statement: 头衔没有意义，在具体场合里赢来的权威才算数。
rows.source_locator: mabrey-techrepublic.clean.txt line 21: 'Titles mean nothing, but earned authority in any given situation does.'

rows.statement: 这两种读法，都落在 Johnstone 那句话上：地位是一种做法。
rows.source_locator: qureshi line 163 ('the same actor can play high status or low status'); mabrey line 20-21 ('the status that one is and the status that one plays')
rows.note: This is the narrator's synthesis, not a source claim. Neither Qureshi nor Mabrey cites Johnstone's 'something one does' sentence. It is delivered as fact before the marker '我的推论只到这里', so only arguably labelled. The repo script.json labels it ('我自己的推论是'); move the label up.

rows.statement: 我的推论只到这里：一个要在陌生组织里取得信任的人，先得看见房间里的人怎样把自己调高、调低。
rows.source_locator: Narrator's own inference; nearest source is Qureshi line 163
rows.note: Explicitly labelled as the narrator's inference, so acceptable. Not testimony from any source.

rows.statement: Palantir 内部怎样用这本书，除了这两位，我没有找到别人讲过。
rows.source_locator: claims.jsonl ov.karp_zamiska_book_via_reviews; scratch overview/data/robbins.clean.txt line 49 ('new employees were given Impro... to create a culture of play, not power'); newrepublic.clean.txt line 61 ('Karp and Zamiska say, are encouraged to apply the lessons of a book on improvisational theater'); mabrey-techrepublic.clean.txt line 20 ('Karp and Nick provide examples... in their book')
rows.note: The series' own ledger holds a third account: Karp (CEO) and Zamiska's 2025 book, reported by two reviewers and pointed to by Mabrey himself, says Palantir gave or encouraged Impro and states a purpose. The text was not read. The anonymous HN comments and the Baffler (2016) also mention the book, without insider standing. 'Found nobody else' misdescribes the research. Suggested: 一手说法我只找到这两位；Karp 和 Zamiska 的书据书评也写到这件事，但我没有读到原文。

rows.statement: 下一集读 Getting Things Done。
rows.source_locator: series-manifest.json assemblies ep02 next=gtd

rows.statement: 看一个人手上同时挂着几十上百件事，怎样不被压垮。
rows.source_locator: claims.jsonl gtd.volume-projects ('between 30 and 100 of those projects') and gtd.volume-next-actions ('150 to 220'); Allen excerpt (palantir-20261006/allen-gtd-official-excerpt.txt line 116: 'too much to handle')
rows.note: Loose but fair. The figures are Allen's estimate for the mid-to-senior professionals he coaches, not 'a person' in general.
